newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Life Offices Association chairman resigns.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Life Offices Association chairman resigns.

text.p: A clash over commission payments to brokers by Liberty Life has led to the resignation of Life Offices' Association of South Africa (LOA) chairman Dorian Wharton-Hood.
In a statement on Friday, the LOA said his resignation followed an internal disagreement about interpretation of an aspect of the law relating to commission payments to insurance brokers.
The disagreement also related to adherence to the association's code of conduct.
"The company of which Mr Wharton-Hood is the representative, Liberty Life, is a party to the dispute."

Industry sources said that LOA members had claimed that the fact that Liberty Life, of which Wharton-Hood is executive vice chairman, had been paying brokers a commission of 125 rand each time they used its financial needs analysis programme, was aganst regulations.
The programme is said to be a market leader in analysing individual's financial needs.
"In the interests of facilitating an open and constructive debate, Mr Wharton-Hood has graciously stood down as chairman. His resignation is accepted with regret," the LOA said.
